To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CPM is well suited for the development of neural network models of emotion and that the CPM can be fruitfully extended to a dynamical systems theory of emotion.

(1) the CPM can be modeled by a neural network, (2) this model is able to simulate the temporal unfolding of emotional episodes, (3) the temporal unfolding can be modeled by non-linear dynamic systems, and (4) this model can be used to simulate the perception of facial expression and the decoding of emotion.
the CPM can serve as a blueprint for the development of a computational model that can be used in the design of affective artificial agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systems approach to emotion and the development of a neural network model for appraisal mechanisms in emotion.

developing a systems approach to emotion that is based on the assumption that emotions emerge from the interaction of multiple components and that these components are themselves the result of the interaction of lower-order processes.
developing a computational model of emotion that is firmly grounded on neurobiological principles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a systems perspective of emotion and appraisal is particularly suited to the development of neural network models.
the CPM is a promising framework for modeling emotion elicitation with neural network approaches, but that much work remains to be done to develop a complete model.
appraisal-based emotion models, and the CPM in particular, seem to be ideally suited to modeling the dynamic processes underlying emotion episodes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a systems approach is a useful complement to rule-based approaches in modeling emotion.
appraisal theories of emotion are particularly suited for computational modeling with the help artificial neural networks.
appraisal-based models of emotion provide a rich source of inspiration for computational modeling and, in particular, for the modeling of emotion differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a systems approach is necessary to model the temporal dynamics of emotion elicitation, differentiation, and modulation.
the CPM provides a useful framework for the development of computational models of emotion elicitation, differentiation, and regulation, which are based on neural architectures.
a systems approach to emotion appraisal is a fruitful approach to modeling the temporal unfolding of emotional episodes.
